why: This checker is the only thing standing between the Makefile and a second implementation of the developer journey, and every way it can fail is quiet: a hand-written table emptied, a derivation that stops deriving, a pattern that stops matching, a verdict computed and dropped. It reported "0 targets delegate" and exited zero when its own list was deleted, so the edits below concentrate on the shapes where it checks nothing and says so cheerfully.

mutations.name: the owned table is emptied
mutations.breaks: The checker's input is deleted and it iterates nothing. This exact edit used to print "0 targets delegate" and exit 0.

mutations.name: one owned target is deleted
mutations.breaks: A target stops being checked because somebody removed its line, not because it stopped delegating.

mutations.name: the floor is derived from nothing
mutations.breaks: The derivation returns an empty set, so the table has nothing to be held to and deleting an entry goes back to being silent.
mutations.find: return {t for t, recipe in parse_recipes(result.stdout).items() if invokes_kmx(recipe)}

mutations.name: the floor is compared and the disagreements dropped
mutations.breaks: The Makefile is read, the table is read, and the comparison returns nothing — the cross-check is present and worthless.
mutations.find:
problems = []
    for target in sorted(derived - owned):

mutations.name: an empty derivation reads as a clean tree
mutations.breaks: "Found no delegating targets" is accepted as "found nothing wrong", which is the failure this whole cross-check exists to make impossible.
mutations.find:
if not derived:
        return ["no target in the Makefile invokes kmx at all — "
mutations.replace:
if False:
        return ["no target in the Makefile invokes kmx at all — "

mutations.name: naming $(KMX) counts as invoking it
mutations.breaks: Command position is what separates a target that runs the journey from one that echoes the binary's path, so the floor fills with targets no delegation can be written for.

mutations.name: the environment prefix swallows the command
mutations.breaks: Same failure from the other side: anything at all may precede $(KMX), so `go build -o $(KMX)` counts as running it.

mutations.name: the recipe parse finds no targets
mutations.breaks: make's database is read and thrown away. The derived floor is then empty for a reason that has nothing to do with the tree.

mutations.name: every recipe is taken to delegate
mutations.breaks: The command a target hands kmx stops being checked; only the fact that it mentions kmx survives.

mutations.name: the exact argument list becomes a substring
mutations.breaks: `up` is a prefix of `up --step cluster`, so the `up` target would read as delegating even with its recipe gone and only its steps calling kmx.

mutations.name: no line reaches the cluster
mutations.breaks: The second-implementation half of the check is switched off: kubectl, helm and kind become invisible in an owned recipe.

mutations.name: a cluster tool is only noticed at the start of a line
mutations.breaks: `bin/kmx up --step ollama && kubectl apply -f extra.yaml` delegates and re-implements on one line, and this is the anchoring that used to let it through.

mutations.name: the script's entry point is neutered
mutations.breaks: The verdict never reaches an exit code. A self-test that imports the module and calls its functions directly stays green while the script itself always passes.
mutations.find: raise SystemExit(selftest() if "--selftest" in sys.argv else check())
